occupation: Economist, Knowledge Management Researcher, Business Author
school: Knowledge Management, Intellectual Capital, Information Economics
legacy: Tony Skyrme helped organizations understand that knowledge, expertise and information can be strategic assets just as valuable as physical resources. His writings and consulting work encouraged businesses to develop systems that capture, share and apply knowledge more effectively.
earlyLife: Skyrme developed interests in economics, information systems and organizational performance. As economies became increasingly driven by information and expertise, he became interested in how knowledge could be measured, managed and transformed into long-term value.
scientificField: Economics, Knowledge Management, Information Systems, Organizational Studies
majorContributions: Skyrme contributed to the development of knowledge management as a practical and strategic discipline. He explored how organizations can identify, organize and leverage intellectual capital, employee expertise and information resources. His work helped businesses understand the economic importance of learning, collaboration and innovation in knowledge-based economies.
laterLife: Throughout his career, Skyrme continued researching emerging technologies, digital transformation and organizational learning. He advised companies, published extensively and supported the adoption of knowledge-centered management practices across industries.
whyImportant: As modern economies rely increasingly on information and expertise, understanding how knowledge creates value has become essential. Tony Skyrme helped organizations recognize knowledge as a critical economic resource and provided frameworks for managing it more effectively.
